articleTitle: Synthesis of SnO2 Nanoparticles by Hydrothermal Method at Different Concentration Values and Reaction Time
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: Tin dioxide (SnO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) nanoparticles were synthesized by hydrothermal method at concentrations of 3.4, 6, and 9 mM, and at synthesis times of 12, 14, and 16 h. The vibrational modes studied by Raman spectroscopy indicate the formation of a Sn02 phase. The structural properties of the samples analyzed by X-ray diffraction indicate that the synthesized Sn02 nanoparticles have the tetragonal crystalline phase of space group P42/mnm. From the scanning electron microscopy results, the formation of agglomerated nanoparticles with a spherical structure with sizes less than 10.5 nm is observed.

articleTitle: Classification and Segmentation of Brain Tumor MRI Images Using Convolutional Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: The precise identification and segmentation of brain tumors play a crucial role in medical image analysis, enabling accurate diagnosis and effective treatment planning for a global challenge in central nervous system cancer. In this study, a deep learning-based model for multiclass brain tumor classification and binary segmentation in MRI scans is proposed. Based on convolutional neural networks, the model classifies four tumor types, achieving an overall accuracy of 93.56%. The segmentation model was oriented only to the meningioma class and the U -Net architecture was used. The model accurately delineates tumor boundaries, with a high similarity to the annotated masks under medical supervision. The segmentation model achieved an overall accuracy of 98.54 % and a mean intersection over junction of 81.96%, demonstrating its ability to handle complex tumor shapes and sizes. Both models were integrated into a web application capable of predicting new images and displaying the results. Extensive experiments were performed on the model hyperparameters and training data, and the results outperformed state-of-the-art approaches in accuracy.

articleTitle: Validation of a UV Spectrophotometric Method for Quantification of Omeprazole Using Different Types of Diluents
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: Introduction: Omeprazole treats intestinal ulcers and gastroesophageal reflux. Extemporaneous preparations are one of the primary forms of administration in hospitalized patients. Although its preparation is carried out under safe conditions, there are no optimal storage and preparation conditions to ensure its physicochemical stability. Thus, accessible analytical methods are required to guarantee quality control in hospitals. Objective: This study validated a UV spectrophotometric method for quantifying omeprazole in extemporaneous preparations. Methods: Omeprazole (10 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{pg}/\text{mL})$</tex>, diluted in three different diluents, was analyzed under light and temperature conditions. The validated test performed for the system were linearity, precision, and specificity. For the method, linearity, precision, accuracy, and analytical stability, were tested. Results: The validated tests applied for the three different diluents were within the required parameters, therefore, the UV spectrophotometric method performed in this study is a valid procedure to quantify omeprazole in extemporaneous preparations. Conclusion: Validation of low-cost and accessible procedures for drug quantification are essential, ensuring quality control of extemporaneous preparations used in hospitals.

articleTitle: Virtual Educational Environments in Mexican Legislation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: The purpose of this essay is to approach the legal view in which virtual educational environments are developed, which were exposed to the health emergency by COVID-19 from 2019 to date, and how the parliamentary scenario was responding. The article is developed under a descriptive and analytical approach, where it is intended that Higher Education Institutions have knowledge of the regulatory framework and verify if their educational platforms are developed within it.

articleTitle: On the Procedure of Finding the ENOB in ADC Converters
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: Nowadays analog-to-digital converters (ADCs) are widely used and can be found in various applications that require the conversion of analog signals to the digital domain. Despite the abundance of literature on ADC design, there is little information regarding the accurate characterization of these devices, resulting in common errors when simulating and determining their key parameters, especially for the most important one, the effective number of bits (ENOB). This papers provides a comprehensive guide on the proper characterization of the ENOB in ADCs. Also, this work highlights the most common errors during the acquisition and processing of the output data coming from the ADC's simulation.

articleTitle: Polynomial Model to Estimate the Electrical Power of a Photovoltaic System
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: This paper presents a method used to select the variables and degree of a polynomial model, aiming for the best possible fit with the least amount of independent variables involved in the polynomial, this approach was used to estimate the electrical power of a photovoltaic system connected to the grid with a production capacity of 4 kW. The database includes AC/DC voltage and current, electric power, energy generated, grid frequency, inclined global irradiance, inclined diffuse irradiance, ambient temperature, and PV panel back surface temperature [1]. The proposed model has been compared with a monolayer artificial neural network and the coefficient of determination (R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>), adjusted coefficient of determination (R<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">a</inf>) and root mean square error (RMSE) were utilized to validate the model.

articleTitle: Creation of a Virtual Reality Environment for Teaching Applied to a Catamaran-Type Ferry, Detailing the Engine Room
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: This work focused on implementing virtual reality technology on a ferry with the aim of creating an immersive experience for training and training in the naval industry, the experience allows users to explore the interior of the ship and learn about the different components and processes that make up its operation

articleTitle: Homogeneous Photocatalyst of ZnO Microflowers by Spray Pyrolysis Technique on Stainless Steel Mesh
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: Homogeneous films of ZnO micro flowers on stainless steel mesh were grown by spray pyrolysis technique at different time deposition at 400°C. The wurtzite structure was analyzed by Scanning Electron Microscopy, Raman Spectroscopy and Photoluminescence. The photocatalytic evaluation was conducted through UV -Vis Spectrometer with methylene blue dissolution under UV light at 365 nm.

articleTitle: Wave Energy Potential for Sustainable Power Generation in Mexico
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: The availability of an abundant and safe supply of different types of energy is one of the strategic priorities of contemporary society. In this sense, renewable energies will greatly contribute to economic, social and environmental development. One of the renewable energies with the greatest potential is marine energy due to the abundance of kinetic energy available and its zero contribution of greenhouse gases. Wave energy has a high potential for use to transform it into electricity, because it is 5 times more concentrated than wind energy, 10 to 30 times more concentrated than solar energy, and electricity can be produced constantly 8,760 hours of the year, guaranteeing the continuity of the electrical energy supply. In this research work, a theoretical model was designed to assess the energy potential of waves. The model proposal is based on three variables that are: environmental, technical and social feasibility.

articleTitle: A Functional Photoplethysmography Device Measuring Changes in the Auditory Cortex During the Application of Emotional Sound
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: In this work, the efficacy of photoplethysmography system for measuring the hemodynamic activity of the auditory cortex of 5 adults was verified. In which the signal of a photo diode placed in T4 of the 10–20 system caused by the interaction of a beam of infrared light of 850nm was recorded. The light that reaches the photodiode is amplified and sent via serial to a computer where it is displayed and stored. The study subjects listened to a series of sounds that they considered pleasant and a condition without sound. The results indicate that during a period of sodium absence the subjects present a semi-constant basal photoplesmographic signal. And during the time that a pleasant sound is heard, the signal presents a significant increase that attenuates, reaching the basal level, when the sound ends. The increase and attenuation of the photoplestimographic signal that occurs when listening to a pleasant sound has a delay from its minimum level to its maximum level and vice versa. Obtaining a signal with different time constants that depend on the study subjects.

articleTitle: Selective Data Recovery of an Optical Communication Link Using an Optical Band-Pass Filter
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: This paper describes a novel electro-optical setup to recover data from an optical communication link of two different information sources using an optical band-pass filter. This optical communication system is based on the external modulation technique and is validated at the simulation level using VPlphotonics Software by transmitting digital data. A binary data sequence in NRZ format is used to validate this proposal. The obtained simulation results allow assuring a high degree of success to use this approach in an experimental way for the digital distribution of data.

articleTitle: Implementation of an Indoor Free-Space Optical Communication Link Using On-Off Keying Optical Modulation, a Useful Didactic Tool for Optoelectronic Engineering Students
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: This work describes the experimental implementation of an indoor Free-Space Optical (FSO) communication link using On-Off Keying optical modulation for a laser source. FSO is a topic of big interest due to is an optical communication technique that propagates light in free space to wirelessly transfer data in indoor and outdoor environments. Therefore, this proposal allows optoelectronic engineering students involved in optical communications to complement the formation of the classroom. The experimental setup uses an FPGA (Field Programmable Gate Array) development card to process the electrical information to be transmitted that is used to directly modulate a laser source whose central wavelength is 830 nm. The novelty of this proposal resides in the fact that the digitized information to be transmitted is easily processed in the FPGA, which makes it easier and more direct the optical modulation. This experimental setup can be easily replicated in a laboratory and has a potential application as a didactic tool in a course on optical communication systems.

Author Keywords: vhsic hardware description language on-off keying

articleTitle: Evaluation of Emergency Calls (eCall) Using Voice and Video over IMS in 5G/NR Mobile Network
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: Nowadays, around the world the deployment of the fifth-generation (5G) mobile network is in progress and Emergency Calls (eCall) have not been provided yet since are under study. Therefore, the contribution of this work is to provide an overview of how 5G eCall are deployed using both voice and video calls over IP Multimedia Subsystem (IMS) in the 5G mobile network utilizing the New Radio (NR) interface. The article highlights the main points considering the deployment of 5G eCalls in Stand-Alone (SA) architecture evaluating also, how session protocols are exchanged through the 5G eCall session. In addition, the development of pieces of source code to allow emergency services on devices was done. Moreover, Session Initiation Protocol (SIP) messages are assessed and a QoS metric e.g. jitter, for 5G eCall over both Voice over New Radio (VoNR) and Video over New Radio (ViNR) services using IMS. In addition, an evaluation of statistics for eCall using VoNR and ViNR is done.

articleTitle: Assessment of Knowledge Gaps in Outcome-Based Education (OBE) Among Engineering Faculty Members: An Empirical Study
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: This research aims to determine how well Outcome-Based Education (OBE) ideas and practices are known through-out the Indian educational system, particularly among engineering faculty members. The study results from a one-week faculty development training on OBE in April 2022, where the data was collected through an online survey using convenience sampling. The authors applied descriptive statistics to the data using Microsoft Excel, post-labeling, and coding. The results showed a transformation of the educational paradigm in India, with most faculty members stating that their program is accredited and that they are aware of the complete process followed by the National Board of Accreditation in India. The results also cover the perspective of the New Education Policy (NEP-2020) in the Indian education system.

articleTitle: Study on Exploratory Data Analysis Applied to Education
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: Data mining has had a wide application in the educational field. This discipline seeks to analyze the data generated in educational environments to improve teaching processes and predict academic performance. Exploratory data analysis is a key stage of data mining, where statistics and graphical tools are used to understand the data, identify errors, detect outliers, and find relationships between variables. In Mexico, the analysis of educational achievement in upper secondary education represents an important area of study due to the large number of young people who attend this educational level, but also due to the high dropout rate at the higher level. The objective of this research is to analyze, through data exploration, the significant variables of academic achievement of high school students in the state of Veracruz. The method considers from the description of the data structure, the identification of missing and atypical data as well as the relationships between pairs of variables. For this, the Google Colaboratory tool was used to write and execute Python code and import the necessary libraries such as Pandas, Numpy, Matplotlib and Seaborn. It can be concluded that by not finding null values in the data, the integrity of the analysis is guaranteed; Data analysis through histograms allowed conclusions to be drawn about the dispersion, concentration, and extreme values of the data, providing valuable information, since they allow them to adjust teaching techniques, education segmentation, and tools to meet the needs of high school students. top in state.

articleTitle: Determination of the Thermal Sensation in the Veracruz-Boca del Río Area in Solar Cycle 24 from the Correlation of Variables in Solar Cycle 23
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: The Environmental Thermal Sensation (STA) was determined from the meteorological variables Temperature (T), Relative Humidity (H) and Wind Speed (VV), this calculation is performed by algorithms used by meteorological stations around the world. The simplification of these algorithms for the daily use of human beings, could be transformed into minor investments in monitoring equipment, which, this information is necessary for making important and timely decisions at the local level for the care of the living beings of an ecosystem. A mathematical representation of greater simplicity is presented that allows us to determine the STA with the temperature variable. This simplified algorithm allows us to find from the ANOVA (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha=0.05$</tex>) of STACS24Real vs. STACS24-(2) that there is no significant difference between both environmental thermal sensations using equation (2) obtained from the STACS23 analysis, the result was determined with a p-value of 0. 897591, therefore, it can be affirmed that equation (2) is reliable to determine the Environmental Thermal Sensation for any future solar cycle in the Veracruz-Boca del Rio Conurbation Zone, from the current temperature variable.

articleTitle: Passive Protocol Based on Memristors for Lightweight Authentication with PUF
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: In cryptography, some of the main problems for loT nodes lie in the generation, storage, and protection of secret keys due to the constrained resources of the network. The key storage and protection in multi-node device networks often require protocols with dedicated computing, increasing the system's overall demands. This article presents a passive authentication protocol implemented with binary memristors and CMOS winner take all (WTA) circuits for hardware-based security applications. The static storage of PDF's cryptographic keys is performed by a memristor twin crossbar array (TCA), where keys are saved through instantaneous memristance values as logical states <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R_{on}$</tex> or <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R_{off}$</tex>. In addition, the TCA performs an XOR operation between the input and the stored patterns in the array to validate previously saved input keys. With this architecture, memristive crossbars' computational properties are leveraged to implement a lightweight authentication protocol without wasting resources on active processing for the registration, storage, and verification of cryptographic keys.

articleTitle: Some Useful Data Science Techniques in Python to Analyze and Improve City Resilience Indexes: Case Study Mexico
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: In this work we show how city indexes can be analyzed by using some basic data analysis techniques in Python. The correlation of variables allows us to identify which are the variables/features that have the greatest impact on the general index. In this way, city managers can make data driven decisions to improve the general index and with this the ranking of their cities. Multiple linear regression models can be useful to obtain general indexes when the methodology to assign indexes is unknown while simple linear regression models can be used to make future projections that allow us to take measures to improve the performance of cities.

articleTitle: Development of an Autonomous Mobile Robot Mechatronic System at Scale for Industrial Logistics in Warehouses
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: Autonomous Mobile Robots - also known as AMRs - nowadays are becoming part of multiple automated systems in the industry. That is why this project presents a different approach for the automatization regarding the transfer and relocation of materials employing AMRs. Developing a scale prototype that, through the development of a coordinates detection system within a closed space, with the help of a camera located on the ceiling of said space through QR codes, it will be able to follow a path to simulate the behavior that they would have in case they are implemented in the industry, making use of well-accessible market components. Likewise, it will be a collaborative-type robot due to the control program to develop through the camera that will be able to identify the coordinates of multiple robots utilizing a QR code as well as the coordinates of an external object located in the surroundings which will facilitate the collaboration between robots to accomplish different tasks only by using the detection and control of coordinates to execute their movements.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Energy Storage Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: Electricity is highly versatile in terms of generation, transformation, transmission and distribution, but its large-scale storage poses significant challenges. One of the main obstacles facing electricity generation and supply systems is the difficulty of storing energy during periods of low demand in order to use it later at times of high demand, a challenge particularly relevant in the context of renewable energies. Renewable energy sources have a fundamental disadvantage due to their intermittent nature. The production of energy from renewable sources is not constant, as it is highly dependent on prevailing weather conditions. As they do not guarantee a constant and secure supply, their use is limited. For renew abIes to become a viable alternative to conventional energy sources, it is essential to address the challenges related to electricity supply and energy storage. This paper will provide a detailed description of the various energy storage technologies available worldwide.

articleTitle: Synthesis and Characterization of Chitosan-Collagen-Hydroxyapatite Membranes as Cell Scaffold for Tissue Engineering Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: Regenerative medicine involves the principles of engineering and health sciences manufacturing biological substitutes that improve or replace organs or tissues. There are materials that have been widely used for the development of cell scaffolds, Chitosan is a polysaccharide well-known for its biocompatibility; collagen is a very abundant protein and of great importance in connective and bone tissue. Finally, hydroxyapatite is a ceramic material with high biocompatibility. These were the components of the membranes developed in this work. On the other hand, at a global level, there is great concern about the waste that agriculture and the food industry generate, since its waste contaminates soil water and produces emissions that promote climate change. The egg is a food produced and consumed throughout the world, therefore a large amount of eggshell waste is generated. In this work, the synthesis of hydroxyapatite from eggshells was carried out using phosphoric acid. With the synthesized hydroxyapatite and the other mentioned materials, membranes were obtained that were characterized and their levels of cytotoxicity were evaluated using NIH/3T3 fibroblast cell line. All the evaluated membranes showed a high cell adhesion, results suggest that the use of eggshell agricultural waste to synthesize hydroxyapatite is possible for the development of membranes that can become important biomaterials for the biomedical area.

articleTitle: Design of a Programmable Delay CMOS Ring Oscillator
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: This contribution describes the analysis, design, and simulation of a CMOS NOT-based 21-stage ring oscillator. One of the main objectives is to introduce programmability into the ring's configuration, enabling the oscillator to exhibit a discrete spectrum of frequencies, valuable for data conversion applications. Another purpose is to implement the physical design of digital cells (CMOS <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.5\mu\mathrm{m})$</tex> as a proof of concept, and then utilize the digital design flow (using a library of basic cells) to develop an integrated circuit for manufacturing in 130nm technology.

articleTitle: An Approach to Linear Modeling of CMUTs: A Review
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: In this work, an introduction to the technology of Capacitive Micromachined Ultrasonic Transducers (CMUTs), based on its fundamental principles and small-signal modeling, is presented. The aim is to summarize the equations leading to lumped elements of the small-signal equivalent circuit through the conventional electrostatic transducer analysis; a parallel-plate capacitor with a movable plate, such modeling allows the designer insight into understanding more complex CMUT models. Furthermore, the material properties and geometry of the CMUT are proposed for concept validation purposes. As a result of it, approximate values of 150V and 1MHz are obtained for the collapse voltage and the natural frequency respectively. Finally, the small-signal model is implemented in Cadence Virtuoso, its operation as a transmitter is evaluated, where the model captures the spring softening effect, as well as different propagation media of the ultrasonic waves, which effects are consistent with the small-signal model behavior reported up to now.

articleTitle: Development of a Water Monitoring System Prototype
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: Water monitoring plays a crucial role in safeguarding the environment and human health. This work presents the development of an innovative water monitoring system prototype designed for measuring dissolved oxygen, electrical conductivity, salinity, total dissolved solids, hydrogen potential, temperature, and turbidity. Physically, the prototype consists in a plastic hollow body buoy floating on a body of water. The implementation of the device is contemplated in a lotic system belonging to the Atoyac River in Puebla, Mexico, which is not monitored by the government, and the community that uses it has declared that it is being contaminated. The proposed system is composed by low-cost sensors and LoRa (Long Range) communication technology to enable real-time data collection, geolocation, and analysis, providing an efficient and low-cost solution. The main differences of this system with other commercial devices are its manufacturing cost, its easy implementation, makes use of sustainable energy, and its way of communication.

articleTitle: Semi-Custom HIL Simulation of a Three-Phase Power Inverter
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: Nowadays, the usage of renewable energy has significantly increased, driving the development of power electronics topologies with improved performance. Simulation plays a crucial role in the advancement of these topologies by enabling safe and rapid testing of systems. Hardware-In-the-Loop (HIL) simulation has proven to be a valuable tool in achieving these objectives, allowing control to be tested under conditions similar to its operation in the physical system. Commercial HIL simulation systems are expensive, while custom systems entail lengthy development time and require expertise in complex programming languages. Given the aforementioned challenges, this article proposes the HIL simulation of a three-phase inverter using a semi-custom HIL simulation scheme with Lab ViewFpga as the development language and a CRIO-9067 card as the hardware platform. The obtained solution time is 750 ns, and the error between the real converter and the HIL simulation percentage error is less than 2.2%, considering a full load current of 3 A in each phase. These results demonstrate that the developed system can be reliably used for HIL simulation, offering a promising solution to the challenges posed by commercial and custom HIL approaches.

articleTitle: Design, Construction and Thermodynamic Analysis of an Prototype Parabolic Solar Kitchen Under Conditions of Hot and Humid Climate
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: This paper describes the design, construction, and thermodynamic analysis of a parabolic solar cooker prototype for use in hot and humid climate conditions. The prototype was built using low-cost materials that were easy to find in the region where the study was carried out. The performance of the solar cooker was analyzed as a function of the increase in water temperature using two thermodynamic systems (open and closed). The results indicate that the parabolic solar cooker can be an efficient and sustainable alternative for heating water in hot and humid climate conditions since it produces less CO2 emissions and is cheaper in terms of operating cost than a conventional stove.

articleTitle: Optimization of a CCM Steady State Boost Converter Power Supply for a Biomedical Sensor
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: Applications of the boost converter are becoming more popular in portable biomedical systems because they need to increase the input voltage coming from a small LR 44 battery or other source. This work presents a procedure for optimizing a boost converter power supply for a biomedical sensor. The initial design is obtained by using a first-grade model to calculate the boost converter components, then an optimization procedure is applied based on the Nelder Mead algorithm, which is performed using a Matlab – LTspice driver. Values of the inductor and capacitor, as well as the boost converter's duty cycle and switching frequency are used as optimization variables. Design specifications include the average and ripple input current, the average and ripple output voltage, and the output current and its ripple. Results show a trade-off between the output voltage and the input current of the boost converter topology presented. At the end of the optimization process, the best component values are selected based on the electrical parameters that meet the specifications.

articleTitle: Design of an Isolated Wind-Solar Hybrid System, Applied to an Agricultural Production Unit in the Municipality of Tlalixcoyan, Veracruz
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: The energy sector is intricately linked to the environment. Due to the intensive use of natural resources and the repercussions derived from the processes of production, transportation, and use of fossil fuels. The above, to meet current energy needs and provide electricity to the national territory. However, in Mexico, 2 million inhabitants in rural areas still lack electricity supply. Veracruz is among the states classified as energy poor. Therefore, this paper describes an alternative to supply electricity to an agricultural production unit, taking advantage of the solar and wind resources of the region in a hybrid isolated HRES configuration. The HOMER Pro software is the simulation tool used for the optimization of components in the configuration selected for this case study.

articleTitle: Fuzzy Logic-Based Temperature Controller for a PLA Storage Container
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: The polylactide (PLA) filament needs proper care and maintenance since it is a delicate material. Thermoplastic readily absorbs water, which can become brittle over time if stored in a humid environment. PLA filament storage must have the following conditions: store in a dry place, keep in hermetic containers, protect from direct sunlight, and store in a temperature range between 10 to 40 degrees Celsius. Since temperature plays an important role because, in the city of Poza Rica, Ver., temperatures above 40 degrees Celsius are reached in summer, this research paper presents a new methodology for a storage container for PLA material based on a low-cost embedded system and with a fuzzy control algorithm of 49 linguistic rules, for the regulation of the internal temperature of the container. The fuzzy logic controller presented a maximum error in temperature of less than 1% of error.

articleTitle: Applying Virtual Reality for Port Logistics Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: This article describes an educational innovation by applying a virtual reality simulator called DELIVRIT in learning port logistics. The objective is to investigate if immersive technology can improve the understanding of logistics concepts and give a more interactive and personalized approach to training. A Likert scale survey was used to find out the appreciation of the participants about the use of this 3D platform, as well as a logistics knowledge questionnaire to observe their learning of basic concepts. This study conducted in a virtual port found that participants who used DELIVRIT for port logistics education and training performed well on logistics tasks where they used virtual reality technology. Furthermore, most of the participants reported a positive user experience. The results suggest that this virtual reality simulator can be an effective tool for learning port logistics, improving learning outcomes, and providing a positive user experience. Virtual reality technology has the potential to improve education and training in the logistics and transportation industry, which can lead to improvements in the efficiency and effectiveness of operations at ports and other logistics hubs.

articleTitle: Assessment via SERS of Two Simple Chemical Methods for Silver Nanoparticle Deposition Onto Copper Hydroxide Nanowires
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: Two distinct chemical methods, thermal reduction and hydrothermal method, were employed to deposit silver nanoparticles onto the nanowires. These silver-deposited nanowires were termed “SERS substrates.” Characterization was conducted using scanning electron microscopy (SEM) X-Ray diffraction (XRD) and Raman spectroscopy. SEM, Raman and XRD analysis facilitated the examination of silver nanoparticle deposition onto the nanowires. These SERS substrates were subjected to rhodamine tests to assess their effectiveness. Additionally, an investigation was carried out to determine which substrate provided the greatest amplification of the Raman signal. The findings of this study furnish valuable insights into the efficiency of the two silver deposition methods onto anodized copper hydroxide nanowires. This research underscores the utility of these SERS substrates in enhancing Raman signals, which could have significant applications in various fields such as optical sensors.

articleTitle: Exact Feedback Linearization Technique Applied to an Inverted Pendulum Coupled to a DC Motor
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: This paper presents the methodology for implementing the Exact Feedback Linearization (EFL) technique in an inverted pendulum coupled to a DC motor. This technique enables the control of a nonlinear system while preserving the original dynamics, in contrast to conventional linearization methods. A nonlinear feedback control is proposed that allows a smooth switch, which would protect the DC motor from mechanical damage caused by sudden rotation changes. A comparison is made with the LQR control to evaluate the performance of the proposed control. The steady state RMS errors are calculated. System dynamics are simulated using Matlab software.

Author Keywords: Inverted pendulum coupled to a DC motor

articleTitle: Ros-Gazebo Based Virtual PVTOL Experimental Platform to Validate Control Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: This paper presents the methodology to build a customized virtual experimental planar vertical takeoff and Landing (PVTOL) vehicle using ROS, which acts as a middleware between the user interface and the Gazebo simulator. CAD is used to create the virtual prototype, allowing the conversion to the simulation environment. The creation of ROS plugin, and implementation of control algorithms for validation of the simulation environment is addressed, where the classical PID control is used to test the realistic behavior of the platform in simulation. A comparison of results with Simulink- MATLAB, demonstrated using the Pearson correlation coefficient.

articleTitle: Gamification with Natural Language Processing for Educational Videogame Modeling
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: Traditional education has been based for many years on monotonous teaching techniques and practices to assess students' skills and knowledge in the classroom, which interferes with the evolution and adaptation of education using recent technologies. To create new learning methods using intelligent and digital tools, this paper presents an architecture that uses gamification and natural language processing techniques as an alternative to propose new learning and feedback methods for high school students. The main objective is to motivate students to obtain new knowledge or study what they have already learned in the classroom while playing video games, and for teachers to obtain relevant data on the learning level of each student. As a result of the proposed architecture, a platform video game for mobile devices has been developed, which performs quizzes on specific topics of biology to high school level education. Users give answers through voice commands, which are processed with the VOSK library, and then compared with other options using the cosine similarity method. Finally, an algorithm leverages the scores acquired from video game actions on scenes and questionnaires to synergistically derive a comprehensive metric that assesses the user's proficiency in learning. This methodology was validated according to several experiments, and in future work, it will be applied to control and test groups of students to validate the level of learning obtained using the proposed platform.

articleTitle: Study on the Use of Defect Metrics in the Software Development Process. Flaws and Vulnerabilities
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: The quality compliance has become an aspect of big importance in the development of software engineering, here the term ‘defect metrics’ comes in the prevention of errors, failures and defects in the software. As a result of applying this type of metrics we can obtain quality and more reliable systems for today's world. Therefore, establishing criteria for defect metrics is a relevant step within the components that make up the software product. The main objective of this research is to show an overview of defect metrics in software products. We aim to show their benefits and limitations and the causes of vulnerabilities in applications in order to obtain better built applications. This study was carried out using different sources of information obtained from academic databases, which were: ACM Digital Library, IEEE Xplore, Springer Link and Science Direct. The study recovered a total of 20 research papers that met the necessary guidelines to belong to the systematic literature review; these primary studies were previously subjected to multiple quality tests. The use of software metrics contributes significantly to the quality of a software product, however, limiting factors that interfere with the full use of defect metrics are also discussed. Finding the option with the lowest risk of limiting the use of these metrics and greater gain is relevant to the creation of a software product. In addition to supporting the testing process early on, they also prevent software vulnerabilities due to their nature and incorporation in the components of a system.

articleTitle: Speed Control of DC Servo Motor Under Comparison with PID Tuner Control and Neural Network Control Using Simulink and ESP32
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: In this article, a comparison of new adaptive control methods optimized under the Matlab PID Tuner design tool and the Neural Network tool is demonstrated. These methods led to controlling the excitation separately from the TRE-TS3252 DC servomotor, for feedback speed control under Kirchhoff's law. Said servomotor is part of a robotic system, and due to its obsolescence of both the DC servomotor and the manufacturer's controller, it requires readaptation of a new control system. These modern techniques improve the speed responses of the DC servo motor, using the ESP32 micro controller and the BTS7960 driver controller. Results were obtained in real-time simulation to validate the influence and performances of the PID Turner and Neural Network control methods, giving dynamic behavior parameters obtained from the Neural Network controller more acceptable compared to the PID Turner controller.

articleTitle: Drone Grand Prix: Educational Robotics Competitions Using Drones with First-Person View (FPV)
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: This project is born out of the actions of the Educational Model Tec21, of Tecnológico de Monterrey, where our students work on the solution of challenges and projects. Professors from the center-south region organized a series of speed drone piloting and maneuverability competitions as an introduction to unmanned aircraft technology. Multi-campus students, being drone pilots, develop skills both in the virtual environment of the “DRL Simulator” and in obstacle races implemented in the first person using the “EMAX Tinyhawk III” platform. These events aim to motivate students to learn about drone technology, encourage them to develop precision flight skills, and provide teachers, both inside and outside traditional classrooms, with a fundamental structure to increase the quantity and quality of technological education. As a result of the activity, significant learning, and a considerable increase in the motivation of the students to use the knowledge practically and help their scout triumph in the competition were generated.

articleTitle: Execution-Times Measurement of an Embedded Real-Time Control System for Stationary Flight in a Quadrotor-Type UAV
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: This work presents the real-time simulation carried out on the Raspberry Pi 2 model B® embedded computer (EC) of the kinematic model of a quadrotor-type Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) and its control system for steady-state flight. The simulated quadrotor's mathematical model has been carried out according to Euler-Lagrange formalism, obtaining a deterministic, non-linear, and unstable model which describes the translation and orientation kinematics of the UAV. To achieve the design of the aircraft control system, the non-linear model has been linearized, concretizing a linear model expressed in state space. Considering this linear model, four proportional-integral-derivative (PID) controllers have been tuned using the root locus technique in the continuous time domain. These controllers work together, thus forming the control system for the quadrotor's stationary flight. To manipulate the aircraft's orientation, three of the mentioned PID controllers are used; for elevation, the PID remaining controller is used. To perform the real-time embedded simulation, five real-time tasks (RTT) have been programmed: one dedicated to the simulation of the aircraft kinematics and four dedicated to the simulation of the control system.

articleTitle: Bioelectricity Generation with Microbial Fuel Cells in Constructed Wetlands for Wastewater Treatment
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: This research analyzes and examines the effects of bioelectricity generation using the integration of two technologies, the first is Microbial Fuel Cells (MFC) and the second is Constructed Wetlands (CW), both technologies are considered emerging and are highly compatible as they contain microorganisms for their processes, with the first one electricity is obtained and simultaneously with the second one wastewater is treated, so it is considered a source of green energy with a wide potential to be sustainable and affordable, The resulting MFC-CW hybridization required electrodes, electrogenic microorganisms among others, hydrophytic plants in this case Canna hybrids and Heliconia bihay, the filtering material was volcanic rock known as red Tezontle and the substrate was domestic wastewater, the research presents results based on the performance of the electrodes with respect to the power density in mW/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, the study was conducted in Misantla, located in the north-central mountainous area of the state of Veracruz, Mexico (19° 56'N and 96° 51'W).

articleTitle: Computer Vision-Based QR Code Detection for Manipulation of a DC Motor in Semi-Controlled Environments
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: The present research work carries out the design and implementation of a computer vision algorithm supported by image pre-processing techniques to improve the QR (Quick Response) code detection rate efficiency in a semi-controlled environment. The proposed algorithm is implemented in an embedded system using a Raspberry Pi model4B+ microcomputer to manipulate a DC motor that emulates the change in direction in a mobile robot. For greater precision and simplicity, the encoded data of the QR code are 1 and 0, which allow turning to the right or left, respectively, on the DC motor. To complement the embedded system, a Raspberry camera, and a control module (current regulator) for the DC motor are used. Finally, efficiency tests are carried out with the proposed algorithm, where the idea is to obtain a lower error factor compared to the tests carried out in classical algorithms that do not have image pre- processing stages. These tests are carried out in a semi-controlled environment, varying the luminosity and distance to detect the QR code. Once the objective is reached, the best light and distance conditions are proposed for detection, allowing the general system to be versatile and fast.

articleTitle: A Review of Earth to Air Heat Exchangers in Region Warms Since 2000: Influence of Earth's Temperature
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: The cooling demand of buildings worldwide is intensive, in addition to the fact that it has become one of the factors with the greatest incidence in the global climate emergency, in principle due to the processes of conversion and generation of energy and on a secondary level due to the disproportionate use of it in active cooling and heating systems. As a result of the concern, thermal engineering has intensified research activity on techniques that allow providing thermal comfort to individuals, especially in-built spaces. In this review of the subject that covers the last 23 years, the conceptual definitions of thermal comfort have been documented, some of the techniques to achieve it from the perspectives of engineering and architecture, within these the technique of cooling and heating by heat exchangers is included. geothermal heat (air-earth and air-water). The influence of this type of heat exchangers has played a significant role in hot places, which is why the relevant contributions of studies that have generated information on the subject in these regions of the world are included, likewise they have been identified and as a way of contribution to knowledge the authors have established the influences of soil temperature and presence of groundwater towards these systems. Finally, the regulatory documents and standards on indoor thermal comfort, ventilation and air conditioning systems that are related to the design of geothermal heat exchangers are presented.

articleTitle: Recommendations of Security Controls Using Threat Modeling in Information Systems in Higher Education Institutions
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: In Higher Education Institutions (HEIs) more and more information systems are used to automate their educational, administrative, or strategic processes. The information systems process, transmit and store a large amount of information on the processes and personal data of workers and students, which is why the information systems in HEIs have become the target of malicious people to obtain information easily and cause damage. Identifying threats to which information systems in HEIs are exposed will allow them to identify some security controls that must be implemented to reduce level of risk. This document presents recommendation of security controls determined from the use of threat modeling.

articleTitle: Integration of Sensors for Monitoring and Analysis of Photovoltaic and Atmospheric Parameters
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: This study focuses on the impact of local atmospheric conditions on photovoltaic panels and their effect on power generation. The study aimed to develop multiple linear regression models that relate meteorological variables, dust, and the panel's output parameters with its generated power. An experiment was conducted using two identical photovoltaic panels installed in Mexicali, Baja California, Mexico; one panel was kept clean and the other dirty, and both were exposed to the arid conditions characterizing the region. These photovoltaic systems were integrated with a weather station, radiometric sensors, and a dust collection mechanism. Meteorological parameters, short-wave radiation, and the amount of dust deposited, were measured. The results indicated that dust accumulation reduces energy generation efficiency in photovoltaic panels and increases the reflection of short-wave radiation. Linear regression was used to quantify the influence of the parameters on the power generated by the dirty panel, which amounted to between 57% and 94 % for the atmospheric parameters involved.

articleTitle: Fingerprinting: Tiktok Analysis of Network Traffic Using Data Capture Tools
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: Cybersecurity is fundamental nowadays, both in industrial environments as well as in homes and social networks. It is of vital importance due to the fact that sensitive information is constantly being entered into computing devices, which are easily accessible to cybercriminals when there is insufficient computer security, lack of resources or simply out of ignorance or the assumption that one is insignificant as a target. Therefore, this article aims to delve into the privacy policies and understand the data that is sent from an Android mobile device to the servers of the social network called TikTok. Understanding how personal information is handled and protected is critical in an era where the digital landscape is intertwined with our daily lives. By examining the mechanisms and protocols used by platforms such as TikTok, we can gain insight into potential risks and vulnerabilities that may arise in the process. By fostering a deeper understanding of privacy and data security practices in relation to popular apps and platforms, individuals can make informed decisions about their digital footprint and take proactive steps to protect their personal information.

articleTitle: Neutrality Internet Access; Evolution and Challenges
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: The Neutrality in the Internet access regulation must include more than just the Network Neutrality. There are other functional blocks that could impact over the neutrality concept, such as the mobile device (hardware) and their associated software (operating system, applications, browsers, etc.) This document presents a functional analysis focused on the functional blocks on the Internet access, pointing out their main characteristics and functionalities. An overview of the characteristics of this value chain in Mexico is shown, highlighting some relevant characteristics in the Mexican market. Likewise, considerations are made regarding the above lines of action and recommendations.

articleTitle: Electroosmotic Flow of Two Eyring Fluids in a Microchannel Under Non-Newtonian Hydrodynamic Slip Conditions
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: Because of the fast technological advancement that has occurred in recent years in the area of MEMS (Micro- Electro- MechanicalSystems), materials that were not previously considered for their use are now emerging as validated manufacturing options. Among these materials, hydrophobic polymers stand out due to the relationship between the material's hydrophobicity and the sliding velocity that the fluid develops on the microchannel wall. This phenomenon, known as slip velocity, which we now know occurs on the microscale, has been relatively underexplored in the literature. It is for this reason that the present research focuses on the flow of two non-Newtonian, immiscible and completely developed fluids in a microchannel of parallel flat plates generated by electroosmosis. The mathematical model for the characterization of the steady-state flow field is based on the Poisson-Boltzmann equation and the Cauchy momentum equation. Each fluid has independent electrical and physical properties and is composed of a mixture between a fluid that exhibits viscoelastic behaviour following the Eyring fluid rheological model and an electrolyte. In this case, the microchannel walls are dielectric and the fluids are conductive, resulting in electric double layers at the liquid-liquid and solid- liquid interfaces. As a result, the flow field is governed by interfacial electrostatic conditions, and Navier slip conditions are considered based on the selected rheological model. The analytical results are centered on the description the velocity profiles as a function of a set of dimensionless parameters arising from the mathematical characterization. “

articleTitle: Synthesis and Insecticidal Activity of Nitroguanidines Featuring $R$- and $S$-Proline
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: Fresh neonicotinoid derivatives were crafted by utilizing R- and S-proline amino acids as foundational materials. These compounds were subjected to IH characterization and subsequently evaluated for their efficacy as insecticides against various pests: Xyleborus ferrugineus, Galleria m ellon ella (caterpillar), Xyleborus affinis, Sitophilus zeamais, and Xylosandrus morigerus. The <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R$</tex> enantiomer outperformed dinotefuran at equivalent concentrations in terms of insecticidal activity, causing fatality rates of up to 100% within 12 hours. It displayed outstanding insecticidal potential, making it a possible contender for crop protection measures in the future. Furthermore, an intermolecular interactions study revealed that it has a higher affinity for nicotinic acetylcholine receptors than the S enantiomer, which is due to stable - contacts. This work introduces neonicotinoid derivatives with potent insecticidal properties, emphasizing the exceptional effectiveness of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R$</tex> enantiomer, and compound R-(7) stands out as a promising lead insecticide, offering insights for advancing sustainable pest management and crop protection practices.

articleTitle: Proposal of an Instrument to Evaluate Teaching Performance in Virtual Mode
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: The quality of teaching is a key factor; educational modalities need to develop reliable mechanisms and rigorous evaluations to identify the strengths and weaknesses of teachers. The virtual modality is one that requires the construction of digital thematic content in accordance with the learning scenario itself; given its complexity and to verify that the teaching-learning process meets its purpose, it is necessary to propose evaluation mechanisms that allow a critical analysis of the teaching work with the intention of improving the teaching process. The objective of the research is to assess the design process and validity of an instrument to evaluate teaching performance in virtual modality. The research approach was mixed, descriptive, exploratory and explanatory, analyzing specialized sources on the subj ect, and characterizing the problem to identify its causes. The results show that there is a valid and reliable instrument, after applying Spearman's correlation, Cronbach's Alpha and scale processing methods, so it is concluded given the methodological rigor carried out that the instrument can be used to assess teacher performance.
